rounds.text: Network People Services Technologies Ltd demonstrates exceptional operational momentum, evidenced by a compounded sales growth of 87% over the trailing twelve months [E16] and a 107% compounded profit growth over the last five years [E17]. This performance is underpinned by superior capital efficiency, with a return on equity of 15.0% [E13] and a return on capital employed of 19.7% [E12], both significantly outperforming their respective sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. The company maintains a fortress balance sheet, being almost debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.02x [E33, E56]. Institutional confidence is reflected in the positive money flow and the increasing stake held by both foreign and domestic institutions [E38, E39, E40]. Furthermore, the stock exhibits immense relative strength with a rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E47], supported by a healthy Sharpe ratio of 1.52 [E51]. Conceded: the valuation is rich with a P/E of 77x [E1], the operating cash flow is negative [E30, E31], and promoter holdings have declined by 7.07% over the last three years [E37, E63].

NPST is currently trading at a significant valuation premium, with a P/E ratio of 77x [E1] and a P/B ratio of 8.02x [E2], both of which vastly exceed their respective sector benchmarks of 17.93x and 1.21x [E6, E7]. This aggressive pricing is further highlighted by a reverse DCF analysis, which suggests the current market price already demands an earnings growth rate of 26.9%, surpassing the base case assumption of 18.0% [E43]. Compounding these valuation concerns, the company’s operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -45 Cr in March 2026, resulting in a poor cash conversion ratio of -1.10x [E30, E31]. Operational efficiency is also under pressure, as evidenced by a 10-percentage-point decline in operating margins over the last three years and a significant increase in working capital days from 31.1 to 140 [E26, E64]. Furthermore, the company faces a potential liquidity and quality issue with high debtors of 195 days [E62]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong historical sales and profit growth [E14, E17], maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.02x [E33], and has shown positive institutional money flow [E40].

The bear’s focus on high valuation multiples [E1, E2, E6, E7] ignores that NPST is a high-growth outlier, delivering compounded sales growth of 87% [E16] and profit growth of 75% [E19] in the trailing twelve months, which justifies a premium over the stagnant sector benchmarks [E76, E77]. While the bear cites a reverse DCF [E43], it fails to account for the company’s superior profitability, where ROE of 15.0% [E13] and ROCE of 19.7% [E12] significantly outperform the sector [E8, E9, E10, E78]. Conceded: the company reported negative operating cash flow [E30, E31] and an increase in working capital days [E64]. However, this must be balanced against the company’s extremely conservative financial position, with debt-to-equity at a negligible 0.02x [E33] and borrowings reduced to just Rs 7 Cr [E35]. Furthermore, the bear’s concern regarding margins [E26] overlooks that the company is currently in a phase of completed capex [E36], positioning it to capitalize on the strong financial services tailwind [E73, E75]. Finally, the market’s confidence is evidenced by the positive institutional money flow [E40] and a relative-strength rating of 100 [E47], confirming that investors are prioritizing the company's exceptional growth trajectory over short-term cash flow fluctuations.

The bull attempts to brush off the steep valuation by citing top-line growth [E16], but ignores that a discounted cash flow model explicitly points to an intrinsic value of Rs 937 against the current market price of Rs 1,772, leaving an extreme negative margin of safety of -89.1% [E41, E42]. Conceded: the company demonstrates high 5-year and 3-year compounded sales and profit growth [E14, E15, E17, E18]. However, the reverse DCF reveals that today’s price demands a 26.9% earnings growth rate, surpassing even the base-case assumption of 18.0%, while the screen explicitly warns that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E43, E70]. Although the bull points to strong ROE and ROCE outperforming sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10, E12, E13], it glosses over severe fundamental deteriorating signals, notably an operating margin that has collapsed by 10 percentage points over three years to 24% alongside an inconsistent yearly and quarterly margin trend [E26, E28, E29]. The bull dismisses the negative operating cash flow [E30, E31] as a minor byproduct of completed capex [E36], but fails to address the underlying working capital crisis where debtor days have blown out to 195 days and overall working capital days have surged from 31.1 days to 140 days [E62, E64]. Finally, while the bull leans on institutional flow and relative strength [E40, E47], promoter confidence is visibly waning as insider holding has dropped by 7.07 percentage points over three years, complemented by earnings being artificially padded by Rs 21.2 Cr in other income [E37, E61, E63].

Conceded: [E41, E42, E43, E61, E62, E64]. Despite the DCF reading and debtor numbers highlighted by the bear, the company boasts a stellar rules-based screen score of 82 out of 100 with a buy signal [E65], driven by massive top-line expansion including 87% TTM sales growth [E16] and 45% YoY sales growth [E66]. The bear's concern over decelerating growth ignores that profit growth remains exceptional at 75% over the trailing twelve months [E19] alongside strong 30% YoY net profit growth [E68]. Furthermore, the operating margin remains healthy at 24% [E26], which significantly outperforms the broader sector's profitability profile while being supported by a potent financial services sector tailwind score of +0.78 [E75]. The balance sheet is nearly debt-free with borrowings down to Rs 7 Cr [E35, E56] and a robust current ratio of 7.42x [E34], completely mitigating solvency fears. Finally, institutional money flow is firmly positive with a holding increase supported by domestic institutions [E39, E40], matching a maximum relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E47].

Conceded: [E65, E66, E68]. While the bull highlights rules-based screen scores and near-term top-line expansions like 87% TTM sales growth [E16] and 45% YoY sales growth [E66], it glosses over the severe quality deterioration hidden beneath those growth figures. Operating margins have compressed by 10 percentage points over three years down to 24% [E26], and cash conversion has turned negative at -1.10x with operating cash flow plunging to Rs -45 Cr [E30, E31]. Furthermore, high debtors of 195 days [E62] and a ballooning of working capital days from 31.1 days to 140 days [E64] prove that the reported profit growth is not translating into actual cash generation. The bull's reliance on positive institutional money flow [E39, E40] and strong relative strength [E47] ignores that promoter holdings have steadily dropped by 7.07 percentage points over recent years [E37, E63]. Finally, claiming that valuation concerns are mitigated by sector tailwinds [E75] defies the math of a reverse DCF showing the price demands an unsustainable 26.9% earnings growth rate [E43], sitting on top of an intrinsic value gap of -89.1% [E42].
